text:
Joel Armia does the unglamorous work for the Kings, and lately he has added goals: four in 21 games, including one on the rush against Calgary and another last week. He plays a heavy game, 42 hits, in about 13 minutes a night, and Los Angeles is a little better on five-on-five expected goals with him on than without (expected goals measure the quality of chances).

His goals are running a bit ahead of his chances, four on 2.7 expected, so don't build on the scoring. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season and in the bottom 6% of forwards for what his team created with him on, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking agrees that offense isn't the point of him. When he does score, it comes in transition: 55% of his shots are off the rush. A first-round pick in 2011 who became a penalty killer and checker in Montreal, he is that player now in Los Angeles. Our range has him around 15 goals.
